question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Tamanna is as ________________________________ with all her projects
solution:
The correct answer is: **busy as a bee**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"busy as a bee"** is an idiom that means someone is very active or busy doing something, similar to how bees are constantly buzzing around working. (बहुत व्यस्त)

 
 
• **Example:** Riya is always busy as a bee, managing her studies and extracurricular activities efficiently.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, Tamanna is described as being very active or engaged with her projects, which perfectly aligns with the phrase "busy as a bee." (बहुत व्यस्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **busy as a bee**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Beat around the bush** (घुमावदार बात करना): To avoid talking about the main point or issue.

 
 
• **Example:** Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think about the proposal.
 
 
 
• **Busy as a sparrow** (गौरैया की तरह व्यस्त): This is not a common idiom in English and does not convey any specific meaning.
 
• **Busy as a tiger** (बाघ की तरह व्यस्त): This is also not a standard idiom in English and does not correctly describe someone being active or engaged.
